For a robot

Yesterday's map (from the before video) is edited with the verified changes only, so depth noise and the corners the after video skipped never change it. Routes are re-planned from the door to each piece of furniture, and every route change is traced back to the change that caused it.

  • Yesterday's route to the wardrobe would pass within 0.22 m of the backpack, inside its 0.25 m radius.
  • Floor it can reach from the door: 0.96 m² before, 1.10 m² now.

What could not be checked

A change is reported only when the other video looked through the place. Surfaces that were hidden, never filmed again, or seen inconsistently are could not be checked, never changed.

How this was measured

  1. Sharp keyframes from both videos go into one structure-from-motion reconstruction (COLMAP), so both videos share one coordinate frame from the start.
  2. Metric depth for every keyframe (Depth Anything V2, corrected for the lens and aligned to the 3D points), kept only where neighbouring frames agree.
  3. See-through test: every surface point of one video is projected into every frame of the other. It counts as gone only if those frames saw through it, and an object only if at least 5 frames saw through its place and fewer than 10% saw a surface there.
  4. Names from instance segmentation (YOLO11 + open-vocabulary YOLOE) voted over the frames that see the object; colours from white-balanced pixels; rotation from SIFT matches lifted to 3D.
  5. Sentences are generated from the numbers, so the words and the geometry cannot disagree.

The obvious method, a point-cloud diff, flags everything the after video did not see again.

reconstruction180 + 180 keyframes registered, 46022 3D points, focal 584.4 px (95.2° across; lens from 14 mm (35 mm equivalent) in the file metadata of iPhone 16 Pro)
metric scaledepth network, corrected for the lens (95 deg vs 60 deg in training: x0.527)
